extracted.intended_audience: PTO management, federal financial managers, auditors, Congressional stakeholders, and users of the PTO's annual financial statements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and disclosure requirements for preparing and presenting the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's fiscal year financial statements under OMB, DOC, and FASAB/SFFAS standards, including accounting policies, statement formats, and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content compliance (OMB Bulletin No. 97-01)
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statements have been prepared in accordance with the requirements of the OMB Bulletin Number 97-01, Form and Content of Agency Financial Statements, and supplementary guidance provided by the DOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB Bulletin Number 97-01 incorporates concepts and standards contained in SFFAC and SFFAS recommended by FASAB. Follow the Bulletin's formats and disclosure requirements when preparing agency financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement components required
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statements consist of the Balance Sheet, the Statement of Net Cost, the Statement of Changes in Net Position, the Statement of Budgetary Resources, the Statement of Financing, and the Statement of Cash Flows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all six primary statements and ensure accompanying notes are presented as an integral part of the financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting purpose and statutory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial statements have been prepared to report the PTO's financial position, net cost of operations, budgetary resources, and cash flows pursuant to the requirements of 31 U.S.C 3515(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure statutory reporting objectives are met and explicitly state the legal authority for the presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of accounting — accrual and budgetary
rubrics_metrics.description: Transactions are recorded on the accrual basis of accounting as well as on a budgetary basis. Under the accrual method, revenue is recognized when earned and expenses are recognized when goods or services are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the statements on the accrual basis while maintaining budgetary accounting to demonstrate compliance with Federal fund use controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAAP for Federal government (FASAB/SFFAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statements of Federal Financial Accounting Standards (SFFAS) constitute generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) for the Federal government as set by FASAB and designated by the AICPA Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply SFFAS and related FASAB guidance when accounting for Federal transactions and disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy of accounting principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The accounting principles and standards applied follow this hierarchy: (1) Individual standards agreed to by the Director of the OMB, the Comptroller General, and the Secretary of the Treasury and published by the OMB and GAO; (2) Interpretations related to the SFFASs issued by the OMB per OMB Circular A-134; (3) Requirements in the OMB's Form and Content Bulletin in effect for the period covered by the financial statements; (4) Accounting principles published by other authoritative bodies if no higher guidance exists and if they improve meaningfulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple sources exist, apply them in the order listed. Use other authoritative sources only to improve meaningfulness when higher-level guidance is absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of significant accounting policies and notes
rubrics_metrics.description: The accompanying notes are an integral part of these financial statements and must include significant accounting policies (reporting entity, basis of presentation, basis of accounting, budgets and budgetary accounting, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear notes that explain the reporting entity, the bases used, the composition of financial statement line items, and other policies necessary for users to understand the statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and disclosure of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose limitations applicable to the preparation of financial statements: they are prepared from books and records in formats prescribed by OMB but are in addition to other financial reports; statements should be read with the realization that the PTO is a component of the U.S. Government and liabilities cannot be liquidated without legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state such limitations and their implications for users (e.g., budgetary vs. proprietary bases, inability to liquidate liabilities absent Congressional action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forward-looking statements and risk disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain information may be forward-looking (identified by words like 'estimate,' 'project,' 'plan,' 'intend,' 'believe,' 'expect,' 'anticipate') and is subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify forward-looking language, list material risks (e.g., changes in IP laws, economic conditions, hiring/retention, growth management, regulations, labor disputes, technology deployment), and state no obligation to update such statements after the date of the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of net position components
rubrics_metrics.description: Net position is captured and maintained in two components: cumulative results of operations and revenue withheld. Net position is the residual interest in assets after deducting liabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report CRO and revenue withheld separately; explain CRO behavior and how withheld revenue (restricted) affects the ability to spend and the CRO balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and disclosure of revenue withheld / restricted receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: Revenue withheld (from OBRA surcharge) is segregated as a portion of net position because OBRA restricts its availability. Customer-paid fees are earned but available only upon Congressional authorization and a Treasury warrant; withheld amounts are deposited into a restricted special fund receipt account at Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose amounts withheld, the legal restriction, whether withheld revenue was recognized as exchange revenue on the Statement of Net Cost, the special fund balance, and the condition that the balance remains restricted until appropriated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of deferred revenue and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Report deferred revenue levels and their composition (e.g., patent filing fees, issue fees, other fees, undeposited checks) and explain operational causes of changes (workflow changes, cycle time, fee reductions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide charts/tables breaking deferred revenue by category and explain drivers (e.g., pre-examination process changes, timing of data capture, fee policy changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary presentation and statement of budgetary resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Present a Consolidated Statement of Budgetary Resources showing budget authority, unobligated balances, spending authority from offsetting collections, adjustments, obligations incurred, unobligated balances available/not available, and outlays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconcile budgetary resources and their status; disclose significant adjustments and the components of net collections and obligated balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Financing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a Statement of Financing that reconciles obligations and nonbudgetary resources to net cost of operations and discloses resources not funding net cost, net costs not requiring/generating resources, and financing sources yet to be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail adjustments such as change in goods/services ordered but not yet received, costs capitalized, depreciation, revenue not generating resources, and financing imputed for cost subsidies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Cash Flows — indirect method
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a Statement of Cash Flows (indirect method) showing net increase in CRO, adjustments affecting cash flow (changes in accounts receivable, advances, payables, accrued items, customer deposits, deferred revenue, actuarial liability, depreciation), net cash provided by operating activities, investing purchases of property and equipment, and financing (e.g., rescissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconcile net income/(cost) from operations to cash provided by operating activities using indirect adjustments and present beginning/ending fund balance with Treasury and cash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity-based costing (ABC) for business-line costing
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress with enterprise-wide ABC accounting to move from managing program costs at a PTO-wide level to a business-line level, attributing information technology and other costs to specific business lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refine ABC models to better understand cost drivers, reduce indirect costs by assigning costs more precisely to benefiting business lines, and compare PTO-wide trends to business-line trends to identify unusual fluctuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of operating trends and major expense categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose trends in earned revenue and program costs over multiple years and present major operating expense categories (personal services and benefits; contractual services; automation technology; rent/communications/utilities; depreciation; printing) and their drivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain drivers behind increases/decreases (staffing changes, hiring, contractors, year 2000 remediation, investments in IT) and quantify impacts on program costs and net income from operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget/funding status of fee-funded agencies and legislative changes
rubrics_metrics.description: For fully fee-funded agencies like the PTO, disclose the effect of legislative actions (e.g., OBRA surcharge, Patent and Trademark Reauthorization Act) on statutory fees, revenue withholding, and fund balances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how statutory fee resets or expirations affect future collections, restricted balances, and whether new collections were deposited into restricted accounts in the reporting period.
